note: Independently rejudged against RFC 4271 Section 4.3: "The lower-order four bits of the Attribute Flags octet are unused. They MUST be zero when sent and MUST be ignored when received." normalizeTransmittedUpdate clears 0x0F on every complete path-attribute header in the session's private write buffer. The four writer-rail tests assert every flag, attribute code/value and exact NLRI, including unknown optional transitive attributes and Extended Length; the clean-flags control requires byte identity. General and route-server relay tests require zero low bits and retained values/NLRI. The real-daemon CI requires both complete peer frames; explicit next-hop unchanged preserves its literal next-hop subject without changing a flags oracle. The core encoder witness covers selected locally constructed attributes, while the final session writer covers retained/raw bytes. The producer-disabling native breaks are not claimed as selective bit-corruption experiments. This verdict judges the assertions and does not claim a new execution or completion of unrelated attributes/framing requirements.
